title: Portrait Cut for Two Speakers
tests: Tests speaker-aware portrait reframing of a two-person conversation without losing either speaking turn.

faults.what: The output remains landscape rather than the requested 9:16 portrait format.
The sampled frames retain a wide three-person composition instead of reframing to centre the man for his question and the woman for her answer.

judge.summary: The output keeps a 10-second office scene but fails to make it vertical or centre the speakers individually.

must_haves.item: The output is a 9:16 portrait edit of the attached office conversation.
must_haves.why: All four output frames are landscape, not 9:16 portrait.

must_haves.item: The man is centred and his face is fully visible during his question.
must_haves.why: The foreground man's face is visible, but he remains on the left rather than being centred.

must_haves.item: The woman is centred and her face is fully visible during her answer.
must_haves.why: The woman remains on the right, including the late frame showing her apparently speaking; she is not centred.

must_haves.item: Both speaking turns remain in their original order, with the full 10 seconds and original audio in sync.
must_haves.why: The output is confirmed as 10 seconds, but the supplied transcript and still frames cannot establish whether both original speaking turns and the original audio remain intact and synchronized.

must_haves.item: The image is not stretched and contains no added captions.
must_haves.why: People and objects appear proportionate, and no added captions are visible.
